newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mir station realigned, lights on -space officials.
newsitem.headline: Mir station realigned, lights on -space officials.

text.p: Russia's troubled Mir space station has been realigned to face the Sun and the lights are back on in the sprawling orbital craft, Russian and American officials said on Friday.

"We solved the problem," NASA official Mark Severance told Reuters at Russian Mission Control outside Moscow. Flight engineer Alexander Lazutkin had toiled through the night on Mir and most systems had been reconnected. Systems crashed on Thursday when a cable was accidentally unplugged.

A senior Russian Mission Control official who declined to be identified said the gyrodines, devices which reorient the 11-year-old station without the need to use precious fuel, would be reconnected later on Friday. The remaining systems would be switched on after that.
"They have fully set up the orientation," the official said. "The electrical systems are gathering energy from the Sun."

Mission commander Vladimir Tsibliyev, who fell ill with a heart problem earlier in the week, and British-born NASA astronaut Michael Foale went to bed around 2000 GMT while Lazutkin carried on working until around 0030 GMT.
He reconnected power systems in the main body of Mir, including oxygen, life support systems and the lights, before getting some sleep himself, the officials said.
